football_evidence.question: Can Kent State’s pass rush get to Jackson Sharman?
football_evidence.assessment: Most of the 2.9-point difference traces to home field (engine constant) (about 1.1 points), which the closing market has historically priced differently. That explains the gap; it does not make either number a bet.

When Kent State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Kent State’s offense averages 3.3 yards per carry, and Sacramento State’s defense allows 5.1 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).

When Kent State has the ball (early downs): Kent State’s offense succeeds on 35.5% of its first- and second-down plays, and Sacramento State’s defense allows success on 43.9% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.6%).
contradicting: When Sacramento State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Sacramento State’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.8% of its dropbacks, and Kent State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Sacramento State has the ball (big plays through the air): Sacramento State’s offense turns 3.5% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Kent State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 14.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Sacramento State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Sacramento State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 24.3% of its runs, and Kent State’s defense stops 13.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Kent State has the ball (big plays through the air): Kent State’s offense turns 9.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Sacramento State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
quarterbacks: Jackson Sharman has completed 123 of 220 passes (55.9%) for 1,249 yards, 5.7 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Sacramento State, and has been sacked on 12 of 232 dropbacks.
Carson Conklin has completed 25 of 46 passes (54.3%) for 224 yards, 4.9 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and 1 interception in one game for Sacramento State, and has been sacked on 2 of 48 dropbacks.

Dru DeShields has completed 124 of 219 passes (56.6%) for 1,484 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in eight games for Kent State, and has been sacked on 11 of 230 dropbacks.
